tool.name: roast
tool.description: : reference-guided multiple alignment of pairwise MAFs (multiz autoMZ)
tool.command: ## Galaxy flattens newlines in <command>, so the work is a POSIX sh script with argv inputs, ## never Cheetah, so the exact same script runs as a dev UDT. ## Backticks (never \$(...)) and bare \$var (never \${var}) keep XML->UDT conversion 1-to-1. sh '$script' '$reference' '$tree' '$output' '$pairwise' '#if $pairwise_ids then $pairwise_ids else ""#' '#if $species_map then $species_map else ""#'

param.name: pairwise
param.label: Pairwise MAFs, one per species
param.help: One MAF per species, the reference as the top row of every block, sorted by reference position. May carry species.sequence row names directly, or bare sequence names when pairwise_ids is supplied.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference name
param.help: As it prefixes the reference rows (hg38 for hg38.chr1). Letter followed by letters, digits or _, without maf or eof.

validator.message: A letter followed by letters, digits or _

param.name: tree
param.label: Species tree
param.help: Newick; branch lengths and internal labels are stripped. Every species (and the reference) must be a leaf.

param.name: pairwise_ids
param.label: Pairwise MAF element identifiers
param.help: Optional newline-delimited element identifiers in the same order as the pairwise MAF collection (query name, or ref__query / ref.query / ref_query). Enables in-job prefixing of unprefixed MAF s-lines by row position.

param.name: species_map
param.label: Identifier-to-species map (2-column TSV)
param.help: Optional 2-column TSV (collection_id TAB tree_leaf_name) mapping raw identifiers (such as NCBI accessions containing dots) to roast-safe leaf names in the guide tree.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Runs ``roast`` (multiz's ``autoMZ``) over one set of pairwise MAFs that share a reference, as UCSC's ``autoMultiz.csh`` does for each piece of a multizNway build::
autoMZ + T=$tmp E=$db "`cat tree.nh`" $db.*.sing.maf $c
Each input becomes ``<reference>.<species>.sing.maf``. When ``pairwise_ids`` is supplied (from Galaxy's *Extract element identifiers* tool, optionally paired with ``species_map``), unprefixed pairwise MAFs are prefixed with ``<reference>.`` and ``<species>.`` by row position inside the job with GNU ``gawk``. When omitted, species names are read from existing ``<species>.<sequence>`` prefixes.
A species in the tree with no input, or an empty one, gets UCSC's stub ``##maf version=1 scoring=autoMZ``, so one piece of a genome split can be run without every species aligning to it.
.. warning:: Pairwise inputs must be sorted by reference position. multiz merges unsorted input wrongly with exit status 0. ``netToAxt | axtSort | axtToMaf`` (or ``mafSplit`` of such a file) gives the right order.
.. _multiz: https://github.com/multiz/multiz
